assessment_name: Q1 Staging Environment Synthetic Security Review

scope.scope_notes: Deterministic lab demonstration using synthetic metadata; no real packets transmitted.

executive_summary: SentinelAI conducted an automated, deterministic multi-agent security evaluation of the specified staging assets using pre-approved synthetic evidence telemetry. Five security findings were identified across the target scope: 1 Critical, 1 High, 1 Medium, 1 Low, and 1 Informational. All findings were validated by Agent 4 (Evidence Validation) against factual evidence logs, eliminating unverified claims and hallucinations.
methodology: The assessment utilized the SentinelAI 6-Agent LangGraph Orchestrator pipeline. Agent 1 (Scope & Planning) established boundary constraints and authorization limits. Agent 2 (Reconnaissance Analysis) compiled asset fingerprints from synthetic telemetry. Agent 3 (Vulnerability Analysis) detected weakness patterns and correlated them with CWE IDs. Agent 4 (Evidence Validation) verified factual support and eliminated false positives. Agent 5 (Risk Assessment) assigned deterministic CVSS/severity ratings based on exposure and impact. Agent 6 (Report Generation) synthesized this final audited report.

findings.title: SQL Injection in Search Parameter (Synthetic)
findings.description: The application constructs dynamic SQL queries directly from user input without parameterization in the asset search endpoint.

evidence.response: HTTP/1.1 200 OK - SQLite error / unexpected records returned

findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements via an ORM or database driver. Never concatenate unvalidated user input into SQL commands.

findings.title: Hardcoded JWT Secret Key in Application Configuration (Synthetic)
findings.description: Static analysis detected a default weak HMAC secret ('change-this-to-a-random-secret-key') used to sign authorization tokens.
findings.remediation: Generate a cryptographically secure random key with at least 256 bits of entropy and supply it via an environment variable or secrets manager.

findings.title: Cross-Site Scripting (Reflected XSS) in Error Page (Synthetic)
findings.description: User-supplied error parameter is reflected in the HTML response without HTML entity encoding or Content-Security-Policy restrictions.
findings.remediation: Apply contextual output encoding using standard templating engines with auto-escaping enabled and implement a strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP) header.

findings.title: Missing Security Headers on Web Service (Synthetic)
findings.description: The HTTP response headers omit Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS), X-Content-Type-Options, and Content-Security-Policy headers.
findings.remediation: Configure reverse proxy or web application framework to send modern defense-in-depth security headers.

findings.title: Server Version Banner Disclosure (Synthetic)
findings.description: The HTTP response Server header exposes internal web server product name and version number ('Server: Apache/2.4.41 (Ubuntu)').
findings.remediation: Suppress detailed server banners in the server configuration (e.g., ServerTokens Prod).

limitations: Assessment executed in synthetic demonstration mode; findings reflect modeled laboratory vulnerabilities rather than live network exploitation.
Autonomous exploitation, credential stuffing, and destructive payloads are intentionally disabled by architectural policy.
Dynamic findings are subject to validation limits of the supplied telemetry.
remediation_priorities: Immediate (P0): Remediate SQL injection on search endpoint (CWE-89) by implementing parameterized SQL queries.
Immediate (P1): Rotate JWT signing secret in configuration (CWE-798) and inject via environment variable.
High (P2): Implement context-aware HTML entity encoding on error pages (CWE-79) and deploy CSP header.
Medium (P3): Deploy standardized defense-in-depth HTTP security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options).
Low (P4): Suppress web server banner version disclosure in production web server configuration.
